blocking_objections.title: Cross-meal persistence requires save.py change — spec incorrectly excludes backend
blocking_objections.description: The spec specifies client-side option copy into the target slot's options[] before setting selected_option_id. This correctly handles the in-session render. However scripts/lib/server/save.py:_apply_select_mutation (lines 67-73) only writes slot['selected_option_id'] = option_id and ignores any option object. After a page reload, the server returns day JSON with breakfast.selected_option_id='dinner-option-123' but breakfast.options[] contains only the original breakfast options. _findSelectedOption(breakfast_slot) at state.js:547-552 returns null because it searches exclusively within slot.options[]. The selected restaurant disappears from the timeline, budget, and exporters on reload. This also affects scripts/lib/server/budget.py which resolves selected options from slot.options[] only. The spec constraint 'No backend changes — save.py is out of scope' makes AC3 ('selection persists after page reload') impossible to satisfy as written. Codex independently confirmed this is a real blocker: 'Without changing scripts/lib/server/save.py, extra payload fields are ignored.' Note: extending the client mutation payload to carry the full option object would require save.py to read and apply it — also a backend change.
blocking_objections.what_ba_must_fix: Remove save.py from the excluded-backend list and add it to files_to_modify. Specify that _apply_select_mutation must: (1) receive origin_slot_id as a hint in the mutation payload alongside option_id; (2) look up the source option from origin_slot_id's options[]; (3) copy it into the target slot's options[] if not already present. Add an explicit AC that verifies the day JSON on disk contains the copied option after a cross-meal selection, not just that the UI renders it. Also extend AC3 to state that the server's day-N.json file must contain the option in the target slot's options[] array after save.
blocking_objections.evidence: scripts/lib/server/save.py:67-73 reads by direct inspection; state.js:547-552 _findSelectedOption searches slot.options only; day-01.json and day-03.json show options[] are slot-specific arrays; Codex gpt-5.5 xhigh confirmed independently.

blocking_objections.title: _isCompatible new logic is underspecified — risks meals-any drop on non-meal slots being accepted
blocking_objections.description: The spec says '_isCompatible updated for meals-any' in Technical Hints but provides no pseudocode or exact logic. The current implementation returns srcSlot === targetSlot. If dev writes the naive fix 'return srcSlot === "meals-any" || srcSlot === targetSlot', a meals-any card dragged to accommodation would be accepted (srcSlot is 'meals-any', evaluates first branch as true, bypasses category check entirely). This directly breaks AC9 ('non-meal card dragged to incompatible slot is rejected'). Codex confirmed: 'This is advisory only if dev is given exact logic; otherwise it can become a blocker.' Codex provided the correct logic: srcIsMeal = (srcSlot === "meals-any" || MEAL_SLOT_IDS.has(srcSlot)); targetIsMeal = MEAL_SLOT_IDS.has(targetSlot); if srcIsMeal || targetIsMeal: return srcIsMeal && targetIsMeal; return srcSlot === targetSlot. This also applies to the analogous _markTapTargets logic in mobile.js.
blocking_objections.what_ba_must_fix: Add the exact _isCompatible logic as a code snippet to the Technical Hints section, mirroring the quality of the M2/M3/M4 pseudocode already present. Provide the same level of specificity for mobile.js _markTapTargets meal compatibility check. The spec must not leave the predicate logic to dev inference for a function that controls security-of-drops.
blocking_objections.evidence: drag.js:121-124 current code; mobile.js:107-113 current code; spec Technical Hints section contains no _isCompatible pseudocode.

advisory_notes.title: Spec says 'day header' shows city but ACs only cover day picker
advisory_notes.description: The Requirements Decomposition R1 says 'day picker option text shows city from accommodation city_context' and AC5 tests only the day picker. But the BA spec Goal section and Bug 1 Evidence both state 'City name derived from...city_context' for the day picker and day header. The current index.html has no active-day city header element — pane title is static 'Day timeline'. If the intent is that the pane header also shows city+day, no AC covers it and no HTML element exists for it. Codex flagged: 'spec says day picker and day header should show accommodation-derived city, but AC5 only covers the picker.' This is advisory because the Requirements Decomposition (R1 AC) is internally self-consistent (picker only); the ambiguity is between R1 AC and the prose Evidence section.
advisory_notes.recommendation: BA should clarify: is the day header/pane title also required to show the derived city? If yes, add an AC and a corresponding HTML element ID to AC10. If no, remove 'day header' references from the Evidence and Goal prose to prevent dev confusion.

advisory_notes.title: drag.js MIME fallback path allows incompatible drops when custom MIME data is unavailable
advisory_notes.description: drag.js:_parsePayload returns {option_id, slot_id: null} when the custom MIME type is unavailable (line 92-93, the text/plain fallback). The drop guard at lines 106-110 only runs _isCompatible when payload.slot_id is truthy. If slot_id is null (fallback path), the compatibility check is skipped entirely and any drop is accepted regardless of category. This pre-existed before this spec but the new meals-any feature does not address it. Codex: 'If custom MIME data is unavailable, incompatible drops can be accepted. PROPOSED_FIX: Store JSON in both custom MIME and text/plain; reject drops when source slot cannot be recovered.'
advisory_notes.recommendation: This is a pre-existing edge case not introduced by this cycle. BA may choose to add it as a Could Have item or log it as an out-of-scope observation. Do not block this cycle on it.

advisory_notes.title: Transport timestamp formatting must extract HH:MM from ISO string, not use Date toLocaleTimeString
advisory_notes.description: The spec _formatTs hint says 'extract HH:MM from ISO timestamp string safely' but does not give the implementation. If dev uses new Date(ts).toLocaleTimeString(), the timezone offset in '2026-06-22T09:14:00+08:00' will be shifted to the browser's local timezone — a user running the editor in UTC would see '01:14' instead of '09:14'. The correct implementation is a substring or regex extraction: ts.slice(11,16) or /T(\d{2}:\d{2})/.exec(ts)?.[1]. The spec hints are correct in intent but the phrase 'safely' needs to become explicit extraction code to prevent this common mistake.
advisory_notes.recommendation: Add one line to the M4 Technical Hints: '_formatTs: return ts ? ts.slice(11, 16) : "";' to eliminate ambiguity.

advisory_notes.title: day_type label in transport callout uses raw string — SKIPPED_REASON_LABEL not referenced
advisory_notes.description: The spec's _buildTransportCallout appends day.day_type raw (e.g. 'city-change'). The existing SKIPPED_REASON_LABEL map at state.js:42-50 already maps 'city-change' -> 'city change'. The callout will show 'city-change' while the slot skipped labels show 'city change'. Minor UX inconsistency. Not a blocker — the user can read both forms — but it is an easy fix to add: '(SKIPPED_REASON_LABEL[day.day_type] || day.day_type)'.
advisory_notes.recommendation: Advisory: suggest dev reference SKIPPED_REASON_LABEL in _buildTransportCallout for consistency with existing slot labels.

advisory_notes.title: slotId flow clarification: drop target provides actual slot, not meals-any
advisory_notes.description: The spec does not explicitly state that requestSelectMutation receives slotId from the DROP TARGET element (e.g. 'breakfast'), not from the card's data-slot-id ('meals-any'). The flow is correct as implied by drag.js:103 and the cross-meal option-copy code works, but the absence of explicit documentation risks a dev misreading the data flow and passing 'meals-any' as slotId to requestSelectMutation, which would cause _getSlotByKey to return null and silently no-op. Codex: OBSERVATION_ONLY — 'the existing code implies target-slot slotId; adding one sentence would reduce implementation risk.'
advisory_notes.recommendation: Add to M2 Technical Hints: 'Note: the slotId argument to requestSelectMutation always comes from the drop-target slot element (dataset.slotId = "breakfast"/"lunch"/"dinner"), never from the card's data-slot-id ("meals-any"). meals-any is only a compatibility hint for _isCompatible and _markTapTargets.'

advisory_notes.title: AC3 'budget updates' clause is optimistic — queueSave debounces persist, recomputeBudget is client-side only
advisory_notes.description: AC3 states 'Breakfast slot shows the selected restaurant, budget updates'. recomputeBudget() is called synchronously in commit() using client state (state.js:492), so the budget panel does update immediately and optimistically. The AC claim is met for the in-session case. However if dev interprets 'budget updates' as 'server-side budget is recalculated and reflects the selection', that requires the backend option copy (BLK-1) to be resolved first since budget.py reads from disk. This is a downstream consequence of BLK-1 rather than an independent blocker. Codex flagged as MAJOR but it is subsumed by BLK-1.
advisory_notes.recommendation: Resolve BLK-1 first; the budget concern follows automatically. AC3 wording is adequate if read as client-side budget update (which recomputeBudget covers). If BA intends server-side budget verification, that must be stated explicitly.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex confirmed BLK-1 (Finding 1) as a real blocker: save.py:67-73 ignores option object and only writes selected_option_id; budget.py, exporters, and validators all resolve options from slot.options[]; reload breaks persistence. Codex also confirmed BLK-2 (Finding 5) as a real ambiguity that must have exact logic provided, with the correct MEAL_SLOT_IDS predicate given explicitly. Finding 6 was classified OBSERVATION_ONLY by Codex — adequately implied by existing drag.js code flow. Codex raised 4 additional findings: (1) backend consumers beyond reload also break (budget.py, exporters) — subsumed under BLK-1; (2) drag.js MIME fallback bypasses compatibility check — pre-existing, out-of-scope; (3) spec says day header but AC5 covers only picker — mapped to ADV-1; (4) budget update AC3 threatened by save debounce — advisory, subsumed by BLK-1. Codex Finding 8 (timezone shift in _formatTs) mapped to ADV-3. All Codex findings processed and classified.
